agent.diagnosticsFeedback.description: After an agent edits a file, tell it the errors that edit introduced, so it can fix them in the same turn.
agent.diagnosticsFeedback.markdownDescription:
After an agent edits a file, tell it the errors that edit introduced, so it can fix them in the same turn.

Only errors the edit introduced, from the language server already open for that file: up to 10 per file.

chat.activeFileContext.description: Show the file open in the editor as a chip in the composer. While the chip is there, sending mentions that file. Remove the chip to send without it.
chat.activeFileContext.markdownDescription:
Show the file open in the editor as a chip in the composer. While the chip is there, sending mentions that file. Remove the chip to send without it.

The chip names the file relative to the workspace. Removing it lasts until the editor's active file changes.

chat.autoSettleAfterDays.description: Move a session to Settled once it has had no activity for this many days, including existing sessions. 0 turns it off.
chat.autoSettleAfterDays.markdownDescription:
Move a session to Settled once it has had no activity for this many days, including existing sessions. 0 turns it off.

The server checks every 5 minutes. A session with an open pull request, a pending approval or question, a queued or running turn, or live background work stays unsettled.

chat.autoSettleOnMerge.description: Move a session to Settled when its worktree's pull request is merged. A closed pull request settles it whenever automatic settlement is on.
chat.autoSettleOnMerge.markdownDescription:
Move a session to Settled when its worktree's pull request is merged. A closed pull request settles it whenever automatic settlement is on.

A merge or close counts when it happens after your last request in the session.

chat.confirmSessionDelete.description: Ask before permanently deleting one or more sessions.

chat.contextWindowMeterEnabled.description: Show how full the session's context window is, in the composer and the session header.
chat.contextWindowMeterEnabled.markdownDescription:
Show how full the session's context window is, in the composer and the session header.

Claude reports what fills the window: system prompt, tools, messages, and the reserve kept for compaction. Other providers show the turn's token counts. The meter's popover also shows the session's tokens and cost.

chat.defaultInteractionMode.description: Whether a new session starts in plan mode.
chat.defaultInteractionMode.markdownDescription:
Whether a new session starts in plan mode.

Applies while `chat.planModeEnabled` is on.

chat.defaultRuntimeMode.description: What the agent in a new session may do without asking you first.
chat.defaultRuntimeMode.markdownDescription:
What the agent in a new session may do without asking you first.

Full access suits a machine with one owner who trusts agents with its checkouts: Codex starts with approval policy never and sandbox danger-full-access, and Claude pre-approves every tool. This is an application setting, so a workspace file in a cloned repository cannot change it.

chat.followUpBehavior.description: What happens to a message you send while the agent is still working: it waits until the turn ends, or reaches the agent at once to correct it. The other send key (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter, or Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+Enter where Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends) does the other one.

chat.inAppNotificationsEnabled.description: While you are using this window, show a notice with an Open session button when another session needs you or finishes.

chat.keepImportedSessionsUpdated.description: Imported chats keep getting new messages from the Claude or Codex history on this machine until you send a message in them from Platform. New chats are imported only when you click Import.
chat.keepImportedSessionsUpdated.markdownDescription:
Imported chats keep getting new messages from the Claude or Codex history on this machine until you send a message in them from Platform. New chats are imported only when you click Import.

The server rescans local Claude and Codex history every minute and brings imported chats up to date. A chat stops updating once it has a turn sent from Platform.

chat.notificationMode.description: Notify you when a session needs you or finishes. System notifications need the browser’s permission; sound plays only after you have clicked or typed in the app.

chat.planModeEnabled.description: Show the Plan mode picker and the /plan and /default commands for providers that have them. Hiding them keeps the plan mode choice saved in each draft.

chat.projectAutoSettle.description: Automatic settlement overrides keyed by project UUID on this machine.

chat.projectGrouping.description: Group projects by repository, by folder inside the repository, or by machine. Git projects are added at the repository root today, so the two repository options group the same way.
chat.projectGrouping.markdownDescription:
Group projects by repository, by folder inside the repository, or by machine. Git projects are added at the repository root today, so the two repository options group the same way.

Repository puts one repository's checkouts on this machine and on connected machines under one project row. Separate gives each machine's project its own row.

chat.projectGroupingOverrides.description: Grouping mode per scoped project key (environment UUID:project UUID).

chat.projectResponseStreamingModes.description: Response streaming mode overrides keyed by project UUID on this machine.

chat.projectTextGenerationModels.description: Title generation model overrides keyed by project UUID on this machine.

chat.pushNotifications.description: Send a push notification to every device listed below when a session needs you or finishes. None are sent while you are using a window of this app.
chat.pushNotifications.markdownDescription:
Send a push notification to every device listed below when a session needs you or finishes. None are sent while you are using a window of this app.

Only live changes push: replaying history, recovering after a restart and archived sessions never notify. A device the push service rejects with 404 or 410 is removed.

chat.responseStreamingMode.description: How the agent’s reply appears while it writes: a paragraph at a time, all at once when the turn ends, or token by token.
chat.responseStreamingMode.markdownDescription:
How the agent’s reply appears while it writes: a paragraph at a time, all at once when the turn ends, or token by token.

Paragraph publishes text at blank lines, closed code fences and new list items: the first break at once, later ones at least 400 ms apart. The end of the turn, a question from the agent, or 24,000 buffered characters flushes the rest. Token mode still delivers reasoning by paragraph.

chat.sendShortcut.description: Which key sends a message. Enter: Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line. Enter until multiline: Enter sends until the message has a second line, then Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter: Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends and Enter adds a line. Where Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends, Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends with the other follow-up behavior.

chat.sessionSortOrder.description: Order sessions in the palette, and pick which session opens after a deletion, by latest user activity or by creation time.

chat.textGenerationModel.description: Provider and model that write session titles.
chat.textGenerationModel.markdownDescription:
Provider and model that write session titles.

Titles use gpt-5.6-luna at low effort through Codex. When Codex is disabled or missing, the server uses the first enabled provider in the order Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode, Antigravity, with that provider's small model. A failed title request keeps the current title and logs a warning.

developer.clientUpdateCheckSeconds.description: Seconds between checks for an available web update while the app is visible. Refresh applies the update when you choose.

developer.deployRestartWaitMinutes.description: Minutes `bun run deploy --restart` waits for running sessions to finish before it gives up. `--interrupt` restarts at once and ends those turns.
developer.deployRestartWaitMinutes.markdownDescription:
Minutes `bun run deploy --restart` waits for running sessions to finish before it gives up. `--interrupt` restarts at once and ends those turns.

Thirty minutes covers a typical agent turn. A session busy for longer is usually stuck or running background work, and deploy --interrupt ends it.

developer.devServerIdleMinutes.description: Minutes the shared dev server keeps running after its last connection closes; mesh then stops it and starts it again on the next connection. Takes effect the next time `bun run dev:serve` runs.

developer.simulatedLatencyMs.description: Milliseconds added before every request to the server, to see how the app behaves on a slow link. Zero disables it.

editor.codeTheme.dark.description: Colors for code in editors and chat code blocks when the app uses dark mode.

editor.codeTheme.light.description: Colors for code in editors and chat code blocks when the app uses light mode.

editor.decode.mode.description: Animate a file as it opens, as if it were being written.
editor.decode.mode.markdownDescription:
Animate a file as it opens, as if it were being written.

Autoregressive types one character at a time, line after line. Parallel types every line at once, staggered. Token streams one token at a time, like a language model. Diffusion settles scrambled glyphs into the text.

editor.diff.viewMode.description: Show diffs side by side or stacked.

editor.fontFamily.description: Font for the editor, the terminal, and code and metadata across the app.
editor.fontFamily.markdownDescription:
Font for the editor, the terminal, and code and metadata across the app.

Also the terminal font. A code font without Nerd Font icons borrows them from Nerd Fonts Symbols Only, so terminal prompts keep their glyphs. Installed fonts come from the server machine (fc-list).

editor.history.persist.description: Keep undo history for closed files in this browser, so reopening a file or reloading the window brings it back. A file that changed on disk in the meantime starts fresh.

editor.history.persistBudget.description: Total stored undo history across closed files, in UTF-16 code units. The least recently saved files go first when it is exceeded.
editor.history.persistBudget.markdownDescription:
Total stored undo history across closed files, in UTF-16 code units. The least recently saved files go first when it is exceeded.

Same ceiling as the retained text budget, capped at 1 GiB because browser storage is shared with every other site. A single history larger than the budget is skipped.

Applies while `editor.history.persist` is on.

editor.history.persistDays.description: Days a closed file keeps its stored undo history before it is dropped.
editor.history.persistDays.markdownDescription:
Days a closed file keeps its stored undo history before it is dropped.

Applies while `editor.history.persist` is on.

editor.history.retainedStates.description: How many undo steps each open file keeps, across every undo branch. Past this number, the steps you visited longest ago are dropped first.
editor.history.retainedStates.markdownDescription:
How many undo steps each open file keeps, across every undo branch. Past this number, the steps you visited longest ago are dropped first.

A state is a run of typing. Each retained state keeps its text snapshot in memory, and each edit copies a map of them: 1,000 commits with pruning took 4.55 ms under Bun in the Editor's undo-graph measurement.

editor.inputRoute.description: How typed text reaches the editor. EditContext (Chromium) hands IME, autocorrect and dictation edits to the editor with their exact ranges. Other browsers use a hidden textarea.
editor.inputRoute.markdownDescription:
How typed text reaches the editor. EditContext (Chromium) hands IME, autocorrect and dictation edits to the editor with their exact ranges. Other browsers use a hidden textarea.

In the editor-edit-context-input scenario, an IME correction over the first word yields Hello日本 on EditContext and hello日本Hello on the textarea. EditContext is Chromium-only; Firefox and Safari use the textarea whatever this says.

editor.largeFile.analysisLimitMiCodeUnit.description: Pause syntax, language services, folding and document analysis above this size in Mi UTF-16 code units (1,048,576 units).

editor.largeFile.minimapLimitMiCodeUnits.description: Pause the minimap above this size in Mi UTF-16 code units (1,048,576 units).

editor.markdownRenderedPane.description: Show a fully rendered page beside the Markdown editor, with synchronized scrolling. Works with either editing style.

editor.markdownView.description: Edit Markdown as plain source, or as a live preview that formats the text and shows the Markdown symbols near the cursor. The Cycle Markdown View command changes one file.
editor.markdownView.markdownDescription:
Edit Markdown as plain source, or as a live preview that formats the text and shows the Markdown symbols near the cursor. The Cycle Markdown View command changes one file.

Live preview formats Markdown in place and reveals syntax near the caret. Plain source keeps Markdown syntax visible. The rendered side pane is a separate setting.

editor.minimap.enabled.description: Show the minimap beside the editor.

editor.retainedTextBudget.description: How much text the editor keeps in memory across the current project and the other open projects, in UTF-16 code units. The current project counts first and is never trimmed, so a large one leaves less room for the others.
editor.retainedTextBudget.markdownDescription:
How much text the editor keeps in memory across the current project and the other open projects, in UTF-16 code units. The current project counts first and is never trimmed, so a large one leaves less room for the others.

Checked at a project switch and at a tab close, so opening two large projects can exceed it until the next switch or close. Counted in UTF-16 code units, which equals bytes for ASCII text. Files of other projects past the limit leave memory and are read from disk again when you switch back.

editor.spellcheck.description: Mark misspelled words: in plain text and Markdown prose, or also in code comments and strings. Right-click a marked word for suggestions.

editor.syntaxHighlighting.enabled.description: Colour code by syntax. Turning this off makes very large files faster.

editor.tabSize.description: Width of a tab character, in spaces. Also the indentation width for a file whose own cannot be detected.
editor.tabSize.markdownDescription:
Width of a tab character, in spaces. Also the indentation width for a file whose own cannot be detected.

Diffs skip indentation detection, so tabs in a diff always use this width.

editor.unicodeHighlight.allowedCharacter.description: Characters allowed without Unicode highlighting. Paste the characters here, for example an en dash.

editor.unicodeHighlight.ambiguousCharact.description: Highlight Unicode characters that resemble other characters. Hover a highlight for an explanation.
editor.unicodeHighlight.ambiguousCharact.markdownDescription:
Highlight Unicode characters that resemble other characters. Hover a highlight for an explanation.

A confusable character looks like an ASCII one, so the Cyrillic а in pаssword names a different identifier from the one you read. Typographic punctuation such as an en dash also counts; add it to Allowed characters to stop highlighting it.

editor.unicodeHighlight.invisibleCharact.description: Highlight invisible Unicode characters. Hover a highlight for its code point.
editor.unicodeHighlight.invisibleCharact.markdownDescription:
Highlight invisible Unicode characters. Hover a highlight for its code point.

An invisible character draws nothing. A bidirectional override can reorder a line so the code the compiler reads differs from the line on screen.

environments.devicePairing.description: A browser on another device, such as a phone reaching this machine over the mesh, shows a pairing screen until a link from this machine pairs it. This machine’s own browser needs no pairing.

environments.machines.description: Other machines this app can connect to, over SSH or by address. This machine is always available.

files.autoSave.description: Save edited files automatically, and when.

files.autoSaveDelay.description: Milliseconds after your last edit before an automatic save, when saving after a delay.

files.picker.hiddenLocations.description: Places, project folders and drives removed from the file picker sidebar on this machine, as paths from the browsable root.

files.picker.pinnedLocations.description: Folders pinned to the top of the file picker sidebar on this machine, as paths from the browsable root.

files.picker.view.description: How the file picker shows a folder: columns, a list, or icons. Auto uses columns when choosing a folder and a list when choosing a file.

files.previewKilobytes.description: Kilobytes of a text file the file picker and quick open read for their preview. A longer file shows its first part and says how much of it that is.

files.readRangeSizeKiB.description: Maximum byte range in KiB returned by one large-file read request. Each simultaneous read holds at most one range in memory.

files.readSessionIdleMinutes.description: Minutes a large-file read session remains open after its last page request. Reopening an expired view starts a new session.

files.readSessionLimit.description: Maximum number of open large-file read sessions and simultaneous page reads on this machine. Lowering the limit applies to new reads and sessions.

files.searchIndexIdleMinutes.description: Minutes a folder keeps its file index after the last window showing it closes, so reopening it searches at full speed at once.

files.searchIndexLimit.description: How many open folders keep a file index for fast search at once. Opening one more drops the least recently used index; search there reads the disk until the folder is opened again.

files.showHidden.description: Show dot-prefixed files and folders in file pickers.

files.watchDirectoryLimit.description: How many folders all open workspaces may watch for live changes together. A workspace that would pass it updates its top level and open files only.
files.watchDirectoryLimit.markdownDescription:
How many folders all open workspaces may watch for live changes together. A workspace that would pass it updates its top level and open files only.

Each watched folder uses one inotify watch from a per-user pool that every watcher on the machine shares (524,288 on the owner's machine). Opening /work took 484,687 watches and other apps began failing with ENOSPC. 200,000 fits four roots the size of the Platform checkout (45,036 folders) and leaves 62% of the pool free.

git.autoPull.description: Pull new commits into a project’s default branch when the remote gets them. A checkout with uncommitted changes, unpushed commits or another branch checked out is left alone.
git.autoPull.markdownDescription:
Pull new commits into a project’s default branch when the remote gets them. A checkout with uncommitted changes, unpushed commits or another branch checked out is left alone.

Checked on each Git status read after the background fetch moves the upstream. After a failed pull the next try waits 60 seconds. The Git panel shows why a pull was skipped.

git.maxDiffFileSizeMiB.description: Maximum size in MiB of each file version loaded for a Git comparison. Larger files show a size-limit notice.

git.projectAutoPull.description: Automatic default-branch pull keyed by project UUID on this machine.

git.projectWorktreeCleanupOnDelete.description: Worktree removal after the last session is deleted, keyed by project UUID on this machine.

git.projectWorktreeSubmodules.description: Submodule modes for new worktrees keyed by project UUID on this machine.

git.worktreeCleanupOnDelete.description: Remove a session worktree once every session using it is deleted and has stopped, including earlier deletions. A worktree with uncommitted changes, ignored files other than node_modules, or another branch checked out stays.
git.worktreeCleanupOnDelete.markdownDescription:
Remove a session worktree once every session using it is deleted and has stopped, including earlier deletions. A worktree with uncommitted changes, ignored files other than node_modules, or another branch checked out stays.

While this is off, the delete dialog offers removal for that one deletion. node_modules is allowed because a package install recreates it.

git.worktreeSubmodules.description: Initialize every nested submodule, only the ones this repository declares, or none when a session creates a worktree.
git.worktreeSubmodules.markdownDescription:
Initialize every nested submodule, only the ones this repository declares, or none when a session creates a worktree.

Runs git submodule update --init after the worktree is created, with --recursive in the recursive mode. Credential prompts are off and the step stops after 15 minutes. A failed step keeps the worktree, and the Git panel offers Initialize to retry.

keybindings.overrides.markdownDescription:
Every command and its keys.

In settings.json this is command id to its complete list of shortcuts, each one hotkey or two separated by a single space. A missing command keeps its defaults; null or an empty list unbinds it.

keybindings.preset.description: The set of shortcuts your own changes build on. VS Code uses VS Code’s shortcuts. Platform starts from those and adds its own keys for tabs, chats and sidebar panels.

logs.defaultTimeRange.description: Time range the logs view opens on.

logs.retentionDays.description: Days of server log files this machine keeps, today included; older days are deleted once a day. 0 keeps every day, up to 60 files.

logs.slowThresholdMs.description: How many milliseconds counts as a slow operation.

lsp.downloadRuntimes.description: Download missing language servers on demand. Off means only servers already on PATH are used.

lsp.experimental.tyForPython.description: Run ty as the Python language server. Off runs pyright. Files already open keep their current server until reopened.

lsp.idleTimeoutMs.description: Milliseconds an unused language server stays alive after the last editor disconnects. 0 shuts it down immediately.

lsp.languageServers.description: Which language servers may serve a file type, keyed by extension ('.json'). Values are server ids in preference order, '!id' drops a server, and '...' keeps the rest. Naming a registered server explicitly enables it for matching file types even without its project marker. Open documents keep their current servers until reopened.

lsp.semanticTokens.delta.description: Ask language servers that support it for only the tokens an edit changed. Saves network, parsing time and memory on every keystroke.
lsp.semanticTokens.delta.markdownDescription:
Ask language servers that support it for only the tokens an edit changed. Saves network, parsing time and memory on every keystroke.

Measured with rust-analyzer on hashbrown's map.rs (197 KB, 11,978 tokens) over twelve keystrokes: whole files cost 1.60 MB, 14.1 ms of JSON.parse and 9.0 MB of heap; deltas cost 1.9 KB, 0.1 ms and 2.0 MB, at the same latency. About 5 of 37 servers support delta.

Applies while `lsp.semanticTokens.enabled` is on.

lsp.semanticTokens.enabled.description: Ask language servers to colour identifiers they have actually resolved. Off means no token request is ever sent. Each server still has its own default under lsp.semanticTokens.servers.
lsp.semanticTokens.enabled.markdownDescription:
Ask language servers to colour identifiers they have actually resolved. Off means no token request is ever sent. Each server still has its own default under lsp.semanticTokens.servers.

Server colour paints over the syntax highlighter's colour. On a first open with no saved paint, a warm server can answer before the highlighter has run, so identifiers take colour while the rest of the text is still plain, for up to about a second and a half. Reopening a file with a saved paint is unaffected.

lsp.semanticTokens.servers.description: Server id to true or false, overriding the per-server default. Turns one server's semantic colour on or off while the feature stays on.
lsp.semanticTokens.servers.markdownDescription:
Server id to true or false, overriding the per-server default. Turns one server's semantic colour on or off while the feature stays on.

Six servers are measured and on by default: rust-analyzer 1.88.0, gopls v0.21.0, clangd, zls 0.16.0, terraform-ls and typescript-language-server. A server nobody has measured stays off until named here.

lsp.servers.description: Per-server overrides: extensions and feature ranks apply when a document is matched; command, env, and initialization apply on the next backend start. Set a feature to null to exclude that server. A running backend keeps its old process options until it idles out.

models.favorites.description: Models starred as favorites. The picker lists them first and gathers them under Favorites.

models.hidden.description: Which models the picker offers, and in what order. Turn one off to keep it out of the picker.
models.hidden.markdownDescription:
Which models the picker offers, and in what order. Turn one off to keep it out of the picker.

Only turned-off models are stored, so a model a provider adds later appears in the picker on its own.

models.order.description: Explicit leading order for the picker. Models named by neither list stay visible after these, in provider order.

prefetch.diffs.description: Load changes, commit files and checkpoint diffs when their rows are hovered or active.
prefetch.diffs.markdownDescription:
Load changes, commit files and checkpoint diffs when their rows are hovered or active.

Applies while `prefetch.enabled` is on.

prefetch.enabled.description: Start loading what a click will open while the pointer moves toward it or the keyboard selects it, so it shows at once. Folder listings follow this switch; files and diffs each have their own switch below.

prefetch.files.description: Read a file and colour its syntax while the pointer heads for its tree row, tab or definition link.
prefetch.files.markdownDescription:
Read a file and colour its syntax while the pointer heads for its tree row, tab or definition link.

Applies while `prefetch.enabled` is on.

providers.instances.description: Your agent providers, such as Codex and Claude, in the order the model picker shows them.

search.defaultMatchMode.description: How a new search interprets the query.

search.maxResultFiles.description: How many files a workspace search returns matches from.
search.maxResultFiles.markdownDescription:
How many files a workspace search returns matches from.

Every file in the results holds at least one match, so at the default the match limit always stops a search first. It takes effect when set below the match limit.

search.maxResults.description: How many matches a workspace search returns.
search.maxResults.markdownDescription:
How many matches a workspace search returns.

20,000 is VS Code's default cap. Once a parallel ripgrep run is cut off, which matches it returns can change from run to run, so the cap sits high enough that this is rare. The server refuses larger values.

search.quickOpenLimit.description: How many files the file picker lists.

search.quickOpenPreview.description: Show the highlighted file below the quick open list.

spellcheck.words.description: Words spellcheck never marks. Set a word to false to mark it again where another scope accepts it.

terminal.integrated.cursorBlinking.description: Blink the terminal cursor while the terminal has focus.

terminal.integrated.scrollback.description: How many lines of output the terminal keeps.

tui.theme.colors.description: Colors for the terminal app: the selected theme’s, or the colors of the terminal it runs in.

window.transparency.description: What makes the window see-through: the window manager, or the window itself. A transparent window copies the whole window through the CPU on every frame.
window.transparency.markdownDescription:
What makes the window see-through: the window manager, or the window itself. A transparent window copies the whole window through the CPU on every frame.

A per-pixel transparent window switches the embedded Chromium renderer to off-screen rendering. On macOS a 1440×960 window then copies 5.5 MB through the CPU on every paint, where the opaque window produced no paint events at all. On Linux the window manager already blends an opaque window over the desktop.

workbench.colorTheme.description: Light or dark, or follow the operating system.

workbench.density.description: Use tighter compact spacing or roomier cozy spacing throughout the app.

workbench.feel.description: How controls move and how raised they look: Flat, Seam, Brisk, Relaxed or Playful.
workbench.feel.markdownDescription:
How controls move and how raised they look: Flat, Seam, Brisk, Relaxed or Playful.

Flat moves on fixed durations with flat controls. Seam, Brisk, Relaxed and Playful move on springs and give controls raised keys, sunken wells and squircle corners (squircles in Chromium only). Under reduced motion every feel uses fades.

workbench.fontFamily.description: Font for the words the app writes: titles, labels, menus and prose.
workbench.fontFamily.markdownDescription:
Font for the words the app writes: titles, labels, menus and prose.

Bundled fonts ship with the app and load with no network. Installed fonts come from the server machine's fontconfig (fc-list), so a font installed there works on every device; a server without fontconfig lists none.

workbench.palette.description: Colors for app backgrounds, text, borders, accents and the terminal. Pick a palette here, or edit its colors in the theme studio.

workbench.reduceMotion.description: Slow down spinners and loaders in the terminal app.
workbench.reduceMotion.markdownDescription:
Slow down spinners and loaders in the terminal app.

Applies to the terminal app: its spinners and loaders run at half speed. The web app follows the operating system's reduce-motion setting.

workbench.sounds.controls.description: Play clicks when pressing controls and changing values with the pointer.
workbench.sounds.controls.markdownDescription:
Play clicks when pressing controls and changing values with the pointer.

Only pointer presses click. Keyboard presses stay silent, and nothing sounds while the tab is hidden.

workbench.sounds.errors.description: Play a short rattle when an error toast appears.

workbench.sounds.git.description: Play two rising clicks when a commit is created, a push finishes or a pull request opens.

workbench.sounds.terminalBell.description: Play a click when a terminal program rings the bell.
workbench.sounds.terminalBell.markdownDescription:
Play a click when a terminal program rings the bell.

At most one bell every 500 ms. Silent while the tab is hidden.

workbench.sounds.volume.description: Loudness of every sound, agent notifications included.
workbench.sounds.volume.markdownDescription:
Loudness of every sound, agent notifications included.

Agent notification sounds (turn finished, input requested) play through this volume too. At 100 they play at their recorded level.

workbench.surface.blur.description: How much the wallpaper behind see-through panels is blurred, in pixels.
workbench.surface.blur.markdownDescription:
How much the wallpaper behind see-through panels is blurred, in pixels.

Capped at 40 px. A repository's settings file can set this, and a large backdrop blur costs GPU time on every frame.

workbench.surface.contentOpacity.description: How opaque the extra layer under the editor, terminal and settings is. It sits on top of the panel, so 0 leaves them as see-through as a sidebar.
workbench.surface.contentOpacity.markdownDescription:
How opaque the extra layer under the editor, terminal and settings is. It sits on top of the panel, so 0 leaves them as see-through as a sidebar.

This layer sits over the panel's own surface, so 50 over a panel at 80 makes the ground behind code and terminal text 90% opaque: text stays readable and a trace of the wallpaper shows through.

workbench.surface.continuousSeams.description: Paint one background across panels and the resize handles between them, so the panels read as one surface. Off, the wallpaper shows in the gaps between panels.

workbench.surface.opacity.description: How opaque panels and sidebars are over the wallpaper. 100 hides the wallpaper behind them.

workbench.surface.saturation.description: How vivid the wallpaper behind see-through panels looks, as a percentage.

workbench.theme.description: App colors, code colors, wallpaper and surfaces, in a light and a dark version. Try them in the theme studio.
workbench.theme.markdownDescription:
App colors, code colors, wallpaper and surfaces, in a light and a dark version. Try them in the theme studio.

Picking a theme sets the rows below at once: app colors, code colors, wallpaper and surfaces. Changes you make afterwards, in these rows or in the theme studio, are saved for that theme and come back when you pick it again. With no theme, each of those rows holds one value for both modes.

workbench.theme.customizations.description: Part overrides saved separately for each theme bundle and mode.

workbench.tree.indentGuides.description: When to show indentation guides in the file tree. Guides take editor colours while the tree is hovered.

workbench.wallpaper.description: The image behind the panes: one from the library, an upload, the desktop wallpaper, or none. None keeps the chosen image for later.
workbench.wallpaper.markdownDescription:
The image behind the panes: one from the library, an upload, the desktop wallpaper, or none. None keeps the chosen image for later.

Desktop shows the server machine's current wallpaper: Omarchy's current background on Linux, the desktop picture on macOS. On a Linux screen the compositor already shows the desktop behind the window, so Desktop draws nothing there.
